Why does Voat use the top level domain of colombia (.co) for its website?
Maybe Atko wanted his username in the domain name.

The more straightforward top level domains for voat would be for example .com (like most sites of this purpose) or .ch (Switserland). But maybe they were already taken or they are being squatted. However, I find "voat.co" actually visually comforting for some reason.
All short .com and .net domains are taken by domain squatters. You're lucky to find even 5-letter domans that are free, all 4 letter or shorter domains are taken.

voat.com has been registered since 2004, so that wasn't an option. ".co" (despite being Colombia) is effectively being used as the new ".com", probably because "co" is used by some countries as their commercial domain (e.g. ".co.uk"). Some will argue that it's even better, as it's a letter shorter.
It's faster to type, but my fingers still hit that m a lot. Muscle memory is a fickel lover...
It sucks that someone seems to be squatting on Voat.com. That website gets so many accidental hits. Probably enough to make a decent profit with ads.

First reason - .CO domains are still not squatted, partly because of the higher registrar fees & partly because it was widely available only recently. .CO was popularized by Godaddy and other registrars as an alternative to .COM - because it sounds the closest.
